newsitem.title: USA: FEATURE-Larry Flynt, a devil with angel's wings.
newsitem.headline: FEATURE-Larry Flynt, a devil with angel's wings.

text.p: Larry Flynt, the controversial publisher of Hustler magazine, has been called many things, but to award-winning film director Milos Forman, he is "a devil with angel's wings."
When Forman approached Woody Harrelson to star as Flynt in the movie, "The People vs Larry Flynt," which opened in U.S. theatres last week, Harrelson wondered why the movie was being made at all.
"My first feeling was 'Wow, why would anyone want to make a movie about this sleazoid'," Harrelson said recently.
"But what he (Flynt) is all about is honesty," he added.

The critically acclaimed film, which has already garnered five Golden Globe nominations, covers the most tumultuous years of Flynt's life -- years spent crippled from a gunshot and in constant pain while defending America's right of free speech in a lawsuit brought against him by the Rev. Jerry Falwell, a prominent conservative Christian leader.

He is a smut peddler and a patriot, an exploiter of women and life-long lover of them, the film's makers say. The movie makes a case for each, but sticks close to the facts of his life and lets the audience choose who the real man is.
FROM MOZART TO SMUT-KING

Forman, who won Academy Awards for "One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest" and "Amadeus," said at a recent news conference Flynt's life was, "intriguing to me, and that is why (the film) was exciting to make."

To play the principal roles, Forman chose actors almost as controversial as their subjects. Harrelson advocates the legalisation of hemp, or marijuana, for use in industrial products. His co-star Courtney Love, who plays Flynt's wife Althea, has a well-publicised drug problem.

But the combination paid off; Harrelson and Love were nominated for Golden Globes for best actor and best actress respectively. In addition, Forman got a best director nomination, the film was nominated for best picture in the drama category and it also got a best screenplay nomination.
Flynt grew up dirt poor in a shack in rural Magoffin County, Kentucky. He dropped out of grade school and sold bootleg liquor as a boy.
The movie picks up his life during the 1970s when Flynt, now 54, started Hustler as a newsletter to drum up business for several strip clubs he owned in Ohio.

The magazine's first full issue was a bomb, but the second grabbed headlines around the world with photos of Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis sunbathing nude on a Greek island. That one issue made Larry Flynt his first million dollars.
FIGHTS CENSORS

But soon thereafter came attempts to ban Hustler from newsstands for breaking obscenity laws. One effort in Ohio was led by Charles Keating, who would achieve his own measure of infamy in the 1980s at the centre of the U.S. savings and loan debacle.

Then came the suit filed by Falwell who, as the head of a group known as "The Moral Majority," was one of the country's foremost religious leaders. When Hustler published a parody of an advertisement that portrayed Falwell as having lost his virginity to his mother, Falwell sued for libel.
He eventually lost to Flynt, but the publisher spent $40 to $50 million of his own money defending himself and the right of free speech, according to the film's writers.

Through more than a decade of battling the legal system and developing his magazine business, Flynt, in his fashion, remained a devoted husband to his wife Althea. They met when she was dancing in one of his clubs and fell in love shortly thereafter.

She was instrumental in running Hustler and remained by Flynt's bedside while he recovered from a gunshot by an unknown assailant outside a Georgia courthouse in 1978 that left him paralysed from the waist down.
But during his years of convalescence, she developed an addiction to the drugs being supplied to Flynt. She later died of AIDS.
The real-life characters of "The People vs Larry Flynt" are not pretty. They break society's norms, and they do not have nice, tidy careers.

Indeed, whether Americans like or hate Larry Flynt is not the point. In the filmmakers' view, he is a man who remained true to his beliefs and steadfast in their defence -- notions as American as apple pie.
